coverage_note: Mississippi has no public-sector collective bargaining statute in the sources captured. Statutes prohibit strikes by teachers and, as far as practicable, by all public employees, and the right-to-work statute bars compulsory dues or fees. The official free Mississippi Code is a script-only LexisNexis portal and Justia refused the capture agent, so text comes from Public.Resource.Org's 2013 XML edition of the Mississippi Code; amendments after 2013 were not checked.
quote_normalization: quote_binding exact-substring is checked after Unicode NFC and collapsing every run of whitespace (including no-break space) to one space, in both the quote and the text extracted from the captured bytes (HTML: BeautifulSoup get_text; PDF: pdftotext)

strike_legality.value: Prohibited. Teacher strikes are illegal and unprotected, and the teacher strike ban and its penalties apply as far as practicable to all public employees and employers.
strike_legality.quote: (2) It is hereby declared that a strike, concerted work stoppage or concerted refusal to perform lawful duties in any manner by certified teachers against public school districts within the State of Mississippi shall be illegal, unprotected and contrary to the public policy of the State of Mississippi.

agency_fee_status.value: Prohibited. The right-to-work statute bars any employer from requiring dues or fees as a condition of employment, and Janus v. AFSCME (2018) bars agency fees from nonconsenting public employees.
agency_fee_status.quote: (d) No employer shall require any person, as a condition of employment or continuation of employment, to pay any dues, fees, or other charges of any kind to any labor union or labor organization.

source.publisher: Public.Resource.Org (law.resource.org), Mississippi Code of 1972 as of 2013
